source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source_reported_historical_synonyms: Petalostemon candidus Michx. (var. candida historical synonym)

morphology_source_reported.leaves: 5–9 glabrous leaflets, 10–30 mm long, linear-lanceolate to oblanceolate, acute to obtuse
morphology_source_reported.calyx: Usually ring of small glands near apex
morphology_source_reported.varietal_diagnosis: var. candida lateral leaflets mostly >2 mm wide, spikes stay dense; var. oligophylla lateral leaflets mostly <2 mm wide, spikes loosen and expose axis

habitat_source_reported: Prairies and open woods on sandy, rocky or clayey soils
cautions: Flora states two varieties intergrade and their distinctness is questionable
Does not establish Hays County occurrence or nativity; do not export to identification scoring without taxon review
Flora p.648 explicitly says var. candida and var. oligophylla intergrade and are questionably distinct; leaflet width and persistence of dense spikes are useful tendencies, not absolute.
